title: Define runtime feature tokens and soft-pinning contract for new open-model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Clarify the set of runtime capability tokens, the soft-pinning semantics, and acceptance criteria for admitting new open models into the Redwood model catalog. Goal is to reduce runtime surprises (e.g., missing KV cache support, incompatible quantization) by surfacing minimal machine-readable guarantees at intake and enforcing automated runtime sanity checks during onboarding.
scope_change: This ticket expands the original intake schema to include a small, required runtime_features list (kv_cache, causal_cache_behavior, quantization_profiles, streaming_support, structured_output_contract) and introduces a soft_pin window (ISO date + duration) that allows models to be routed to canary traffic while still eligible for automatic fallback to a pinned variant. It does NOT change hard pinning behavior for enterprise-pinned deployments.
decisions: Adopt a lightweight runtime_features token set (string tokens) instead of a large nested schema to keep intake simple and stable across model families.

Soft-pin will be configurable per-model-variant as an ISO date (soft_pin_until) plus an integer grace_days. After expiration, runtime routing will treat the model as unpinned unless explicitly hard-pinned.
Onboarding API will reject entries that omit at least one of the required tokens: kv_cache OR causal_cache_behavior OR streaming_support (to force explicit declarations).
Compatibility notes will be surfaced in the console and in API responses as a human-friendly summary generated from runtime_features tokens.
Automated runtime sanity tests (fast start, short-sequence decode, kv-cache restore) are gating checks for admission; failures produce deterministic rejection reasons and suggested remediation steps.
We will not attempt to infer quantization compatibility; model providers must declare quantization_profiles and attach a matching test artifact (small model snippet or binary digest).
tradeoffs: Minimal token set reduces onboarding friction at the cost of losing some granular detail, which will be captured in follow-up opt-in fields.
Soft-pinning increases safety for gradual rollouts but adds routing complexity (additional matching rules); ops will get new routing metrics to monitor.
Requiring explicit declarations pushes burden to model submitters but avoids runtime incompatibilities that are costly to debug once live.
acceptance_criteria: Intake API accepts runtime_features as a list of strings and persists them to the catalog entry; validation returns clear error codes when required tokens are missing.
Console model entry page shows runtime feature badges and a short compatibility summary derived from tokens.
Onboarding pipeline runs three automated sanity checks (fast-start, kv-cache restore, short-seq decode) and returns a pass/fail report attached to the catalog entry.

Soft-pin semantics implemented: soft_pin_until + grace_days accepted in intake; routing honors soft-pin by sending <=10% traffic by default for soft-pinned variants and automatically cutting over when soft_pin_until expires.
Runtime-side metric dashboards (canary traffic rate, soft-pin error rate, fallback rate) are wired and visible in Console under the model's debug panel.
Documentation page (Confluence link in links) describing tokens, expected provider artifacts, and remediation steps is published before rollout.

E2E test: ingest a sample community model with declared runtime_features and quantization_profiles, run onboarding pipeline, and demonstrate successful canary routing for 48 hours followed by automatic demotion when soft_pin_until elapses (demo video link in links).
